headline: Controlled Access and Lowcountry Conservation Check
reservation: Kiawah’s gated residential and resort areas require appropriate guest access arranged with your host. Public Kiawah Beachwalker Park has separate county-park admission and capacity-limited parking, not a reserved beach-entry slot. If full, follow the county’s virtual-line procedure; public beach access does not provide access to private island amenities.

days.title: Maritime Forests and Lowcountry History
days.start: Suggested: 9 AM from Charleston International Airport (CHS)

stops.name: Angel Oak Tree
stops.detail: Stop on Johns Island to view this massive ancient live oak before crossing onto Kiawah.

stops.name: Night Heron Park
stops.detail: Visit the nature center to learn about local bobcat and loggerhead turtle conservation efforts.

days.driving: Allow 75 minutes from CHS; traffic on River Road varies
days.note: Check gate pass requirements before approaching the Kiawah Island security kiosk.

days.title: Tidal Creeks and Atlantic Shorelines

stops.name: Kiawah River
stops.detail: Paddle the salt marshes at high tide to look for strand-feeding bottlenose dolphins.

stops.name: Kiawah Beachwalker Park
stops.detail: Access the only public beachfront on the island, featuring wide sandy dunes and seasonal lifeguards.

days.driving: Local cycling suggested; use paved island trails
days.note: Marsh paddling is highly tide-dependent; check local charts for safe navigation windows.

days.title: Barrier Island Biking and Estuary Views

stops.name: Marsh Island Park
stops.detail: Climb the observation tower for expansive views of the Kiawah River and nesting ospreys.

stops.name: Ocean Course Lookout
stops.detail: Cycle to the eastern tip for views of the Atlantic meeting the Lowcountry marshland.

days.driving: Walking or cycling within the gates; driving to Johns Island for dinner
days.note: Bicycles are the primary transport on the island's 30 miles of paved trails.

intel.title: Gated Community Entry
intel.text: Access beyond Freshfields Village requires a resident or guest pass. Public beach access is limited to the county park at the island's west end.

intel.title: Mainland Supply Points
intel.text: Freshfields Village offers the last major fueling and grocery stop before the residential zones. On-island services are limited to resort areas.

intel.title: Tidal Fluctuations
intel.text: Tides in the Lowcountry can swing significantly twice daily. Plan paddling trips around high tide to avoid getting stranded in pluff mud.

intel.title: Maritime Forest Coverage
intel.text: Cellular signal is generally stable in developed zones but can drop in deep marsh areas. GPS may struggle under heavy live oak canopies.

intel.title: Beachwalker Park Limits
intel.text: The public parking lot at Beachwalker Park has finite capacity and can close when full. Arrive early or check local county park alerts.

plan.arrival: Pick up rental at CHS, stop for supplies on Johns Island, and ensure you have your gate code ready for the Kiawah security check.
plan.vehicle: A standard car is sufficient, but avoid oversized RVs on narrow, oak-lined island roads.
plan.goldenHour: The eastern shore near the Ocean Course offers stunning sunrise vistas over the Atlantic.
